### Photovoltaic panel {-}

```{rosmose}
! OSMOSE ET PVpanel
```

Photovoltaic (PV) panels are recognized as essential components of renewable energy infrastructure by converting sunlight into electricity. Their performance is subject to various design and external factors. For instance, ambient temperature directly affects the panel efficiency, as the elevated temperatures lead to decreased power output due to semiconductor material sensitivity. In addition, the output of a photovoltaic panel partly depends on the angle of the sun relative to the panel. The global horizontal irradiance (GHI) is the amount of terrestrial irradiance falling on a surface horizontal to the surface of the earth [in W/m2] and dictates the potential energy yield of PV systems. Irradiation values can be obtained from an insolation map or from insolation tables that reflect data over the prior 30–50 years. Moreover, part of the solar radiation reaching an object is absorbed and the remainder is reflected. The fraction of solar irradiation that passes through a PV glass determines the absorbed energy. Usually, the absorbed radiation is converted to thermal energy, increasing the object temperature. In this regard, the thermal transmission coefficient of a PV panel impacts the heat dissipation capacity, affecting the overall performance. Finallt, the temperature coefficient of efficiency quantifies performance changes with temperature, influencing the energy output.


```{r pvpanel, out.width='80%', fig.align='center', fig.cap='Photovoltaic panel structure'}
knitr::include_graphics('PVpanel.svg')
```

Some technical parameters needed to estimate the electrical production of the PV module are defined in the following chunk of code, as well as other financial parameters used to calculate the PV panel cost. The commentaries provide further details on the meaning and relevance of each term. 


```{rosmose} 
T_ext = 10 [C] # Current ambient temperature
T_ref = 298 [K] # Reference ambient temperature
GI = 100 [W/m2] # Global horizontal irradiance
size_ref = 11689.7 [m2] # Size of the installation
area_factor = 0.25 [-] # Effective area multiplication factor
U_glass = 29.1 [W/m2K] # Thermal transmission coefficient
f_glass = 0.9 # Fraction of the solar irradiation passing through the PV glass
efficiency_ref = 0.14 # Reference efficiency
efficiency_var = 0.001 [1/K] # Temperature coefficient of efficiency

# Economic parameters
speccostinv = 300 [CHF/m2] # Specific investment cost
n = 25.0 [yr] # Lifetime of the photovoltaic panel
i = 0.06 [-] # Interest rate
```

Accordingly, the electric power output (`E_default`) of the PV panel is calculated considering the effective area (`size_real`), the temperature dependent efficiency factor (`efficiency`), and the total solar radiation incident on the PV surface (`GI`). The efficiency of the PV panel is also affected by the module temperature `T_panel`. The thermal transmission coefficient `U_glass` and the temperature coefficient of efficiency `efficiency_var` depend on the type of PV panel and are provided by the manufacturer. The portion of the solar incident passing through the PV panel glass is denoted by the factor `f_glass`, while `T_ref` and `efficiency_ref` are the reference temperature and efficiency, respectively. The maximum installation size (`size_real`) can be limited by the area of the roof, calculated as the product of the length `l` and the width `w` of the building. However, other obstacles on the roof can also render a part of it not suitable for installing a PV system.


```{rosmose} 
T_panel = (%U_glass%*(%T_ext%+273.15)/(%U_glass%-%efficiency_var%*%GI%)+%GI%*(%f_glass%-%efficiency_ref%-%efficiency_var%*%T_ref%)/(%U_glass%-%efficiency_var%*%GI%) [K] # PV panel temperature calculation 
size_real = %size_ref%*%area_factor% [m2] # Estimated real effective size of the PV panel
efficiency = %efficiency_ref%-%efficiency_var%*(%T_panel%-%T_ref%) # PV panel efficiency variation with temperature 
E_default = %GI%*size_real%*%efficiency%/1000 [kW] # Electric power output
Annuity = (%i%*(1+%i%)**%n%)/((1+%i%)**%n%-1) [-] # Annualization factor
Cinv2_PV = %speccostinv%*%Annuity%*%size_real% [CHF/y] # Yearly investment cost estimation
```

**Layers of the Photovoltaic panel ET**

The concept of layers in ROsmose language is equivalent to pipes through which the mass and resources balances are closed. For instance, the net electricity generated by the PV panel (in kW) is exported through the `Electricity` layer to an electricity supply grid located in the market model. This layer can be defined as shown in the following table:

```{rosmose} 
: OSMOSE LAYERS PVpanel

| Layer     | Display name | shortname | Unit | Color |
|:----------|:-------------|:----------|:-----|:------|
|Electricity|Electricity   |elec       |kW    |yellow |
```

**Unit of the PVpanel ET**

The model of the PV panel consists of a single unit, the `PV` unit, which is an utility unit. It means that its size (continuous) and existence (binary) can be regarded as optimization variables used to minimize the electricity generation or any other targets. To this end, other parameters of this unit, such as the lower `fmin` and upper `fmax` sizing bounds, must be specified in the Parameters tables shown next. Other operating costs (`cost1`:fixed, in Eur/y, `cost2`:variable in Eur/kWh/y or Eur/kg/y) and investment costs (`cinv1`:fixed in Eur/y; `cinv2`:variable in Eur/kW/y or Eur/kg/y) can be also specified.

```{rosmose} 
: OSMOSE UNIT PVpanel

| unit name |type   |
|:----------|:------|
| PV        |Utility| 
```

**Parameters of the PV unit**

```{rosmose PV_params}
: OSMOSE UNIT_PARAM PV

|cost1  |cost2  |cinv1  |cinv2      |imp1   |imp2   |fmin   |fmax   |
|:------|:------|:------|:----------|:------|:------|:------|:------|
|0      |0      |0      |%Cinv2_PV% |0      |0      |0      |100    |
```

Finally, the mass and resource streams of the `PV` unit associated to each relevant layer are defined. It must be carefully inserted each one of the `%tags%` defined in the previous chunks. It is important to define the direction of the mass or resource streams from the perspective of each unit. For instance, electricity is generated in the unit (i.e. direction is `out`). It is important to highlight that the layer for the heat streams balance is not explicitly defined, since a `DefaultHeatCascade` is already implemented for all the units in Rosmose. The heat streams are defined with source and target temperatures, and the respective heat flows (calculated as `H_{out}-H_{in}` in kW). This utility streams are used to balance the combined heat and power generation of the processes and to apply the optimization routine that minimizes the energy requirement (MER) by maximizing the waste heat recovery.

**Resource Streams**

Defining the resource streams

```{rosmose PV_rs}
: OSMOSE RESOURCE_STREAMS PV

|layer      |direction|value                |
|:----------|:--------|:--------------------|
|Electricity|out      |%E_default%          |
```
